references.text: The context of this gathering: All Israel gathered as one man, from Dan to Be'er-Sheba, at Mizpah ([ref:Judg 20:1-2|Judges 20:1-2]). Verse 11 repeats and emphasizes this unity as they assemble against the city.

The people rose up as one man and said that no one should go home ([ref:Judg 20:8|Judges 20:8]). The expression "as one man" (כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד) is repeated in verse 11 to show Israel's unity in the matter against Gibeah.
In [ref:Josh 9:2|Joshua 9:2], the kings gather to fight against Joshua and Israel "in a united band" – a similar motif of gathering for a common battle.

In [ref:1 Sam 11:7|1 Samuel 11:7], Saul sent pieces of oxen throughout all Israel, and the people went out "as one man" (כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד) – the same expression for national unity in the face of a crisis.
In [ref:Ezra 3:9|Ezra 3:9], it is stated that the people stood together as one (the חֲבֵרִים motif) to work on the Lord's house – fellowship and unity in a common task.
The expression "as one man" is also used regarding Gideon's men ([ref:Judg 6:16|Judges 6:16]), where the Lord assures victory when Israel stands united.
In [ref:Neh 8:1|Nehemiah 8:1], all the people gathered "as one man" (כְּאִישׁ אֶחָד) in the square before the Water Gate – the same Hebrew expression for unity in God's people's assembly.
Israel joined themselves to Baal-Peor, and the Lord's anger was kindled ([ref:Num 25:1-3|Numbers 25:1-3]). As in Judges 20, Israel gathers to deal with sin in their midst.
In [ref:Judg 21:5|Judges 21:5], Israel asks who did not come to the assembly, showing that the united gathering described in 20:11 was seen as a serious obligation.
